title: Why LGUs maintain local household data | Spatialdom Insights
description: How current household information can support local planning, service follow-up, and evidence-based decisions without overlooking privacy.
heading: Why LGUs maintain local household data
intro: Local programs need a picture of who lives where and which needs are changing. Reliable household information can help, provided collection and use stay tied to a legitimate purpose.

sections.heading: Use evidence to locate needs
paragraphs: Aggregate household data can help an LGU compare areas, identify gaps in basic services, and plan follow-up. CPD describes RBIM as household demographic and socioeconomic data that can support local planning and help track population movement.

Named records can support authorized case work, but they should not be the default view for every planning question. Decide whether an aggregate map, count, or individual record is actually needed for each task.

sections.heading: Keep information current enough to use
paragraphs: A record collected once becomes less useful as families move and circumstances change. Assign an owner for updates, record the date and source of a change, and give staff a way to flag uncertain or duplicate entries. Review the quality of data before using it to prioritize services.
Different offices may hold overlapping records. Agree on identifiers and a correction process before combining them; copying files into a shared database does not resolve conflicting facts.

sections.heading: Make privacy part of the workflow
paragraphs: Tell residents the purpose of collection and who may receive their information. Limit access and sharing to authorized purposes and keep retention rules clear. CPD's RBIM guidance calls for barangay privacy guidelines because the registry contains residents' personal information.
